summary: Martha Lile Love was an Indologist. She earned a B.A. from the University of Toronto before pursuing further studies at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher who studied at Wellesley College, NYU (B.A.), Harvard (M.A.), and under Bernard Williams. She held positions at Harvard, Brown, Oxford, and was appointed Ernst Freund Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Martin Baumann is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Leibniz University Hannover and a Habilitation at the University of Leipzig, and became Professor and seminar director at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

Martin Brauen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Delhi, earned a doctorate from the University of Zurich, held posts at Zurich's Ethnographic Museum from 1975, and was chief curator at the Rubin Museum.

Martin Collcutt works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Fitzwilliam College, the University of Cambridge, and Harvard (Ph.D.). After teaching in Japan, he served at Princeton University from 1975 to 2015 as East Asian Studies Program Director.

Martin Delhey is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and earned his PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. He has held positions at Hamburg, Göttingen, Ryukoku University, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Martin Gluckman works in computational Indology. He has held posts at the Sanskrit Research Institute (attested 2024) and the Peoples' Friendship University of Russia (attested 2025).
Martin Gusinde studied at the University of Vienna (~1923–1926). He later held a position at the Catholic University of America (~1949–1957).

Martin Haug was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen (Ph.D.), Göttingen, and Bonn under scholars including Rudolf von Roth. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1859–1866) and the University of Munich (1868).

Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Rickert and Edmund Husserl. He held academic posts at Freiburg (1915–1923, 1936–1940) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

Martin Joachim Kümmel is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranianist. He studied at the universities of Marburg and Freiburg, completing his PhD and Habilitation under Eva Tichy and others. He worked at Freiburg (~1999–2008) and took a chair at Jena in 2013.

Martin Johannes Hammerich was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen and under A. W. von Schlegel and H. H. Wilson. He taught Sanskrit at Copenhagen (1841–1844) and served as principal of Borgerdydskolen i Christianshavn.

Martin King Whyte is a sinologist and sociologist. He studied at Cornell (B.A.) and Harvard (M.A., Ph.D.), and held academic posts at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University (1994–2000), and Harvard (emeritus 2000).
Martin Kraatz is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under Wilhelm Rau and succeeded Käthe Neumann in 1968.

Martin Lehnert is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Freiburg and was attested as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich in 2016.

Martin Lowenthal is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Mills is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Edinburgh (1992–1997), lectured at the University of Sussex (1997–2000), and held a Senior Lectureship and Chair at the University of Aberdeen.
Martin Novosad was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied as a disciple under Nyanatiloka Mahathera in 1938. In 1940, he served as leader of Verdant Hermitage.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen, Humboldt, Heidelberg (Promotion 1973), and Munich (Habilitation 1990). He held long-term professorships at the University of Chicago and taught at the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies.

Martin Schultze was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Halle in 1855. He later served as Director of Höhere Töchterschule in Cüstrin (1869–1877) and Rector of Theodor-Mommsen-Schule (1877–1885).
